quote: In relative terms, StoneDB's bulk-insert throughput was about 54 percent higher than KVLite's.
problem: Arithmetic error. A2 gives 348 vs 212 thousand ops/s, which is about 64 percent higher (348/212 = 1.64), not 54.

quote: Marlin's higher write throughput comes from its batched write-ahead log, which groups concurrent writes into a single append.
problem: Causal attribution not supported. A1 says no profiler, tracing or ablation runs were collected for any store; A7 only quotes design documentation.

quote: Marlin's write advantage holds regardless of storage hardware or durability settings.
problem: Overgeneralised. A1 shows one machine, one hardware configuration and one durability setting (fsync every 1,000 writes), and per-write fsync was not tested.

quote: Marlin also serves random reads faster than StoneDB.
problem: Overstated. A2 medians are 417 vs 402 with overlapping ranges (391-426 vs 395-410). The report treats an overlapping gap as unresolved in its 100M section, so the same standard applies here.

quote: Under the mixed workload, KVLite's median p99 latency was 4.2 ms, the worst of the three, against 3.1 ms for StoneDB and 2.9 ms for Marlin.
problem: Wrong figure. A3 gives KVLite's median p99 as 4.8 ms (range 4.5-5.2), not 4.2 ms.

quote: StoneDB sustains its mixed-workload throughput over long-running operation.
problem: Unsupported. A1 says the longest run was 6 minutes including warm-up and no soak or multi-hour run was performed. A5 covers only five minutes.

quote: Marlin's own documentation presents it as the right engine for write-intensive systems generally.
problem: Misrepresents A7. The README says Marlin is designed for write-intensive workloads whose reads mostly touch recently written keys. The body drops that qualifier and overstates it as the right engine generally.

quote: Wray kept a continuous day-by-day record of the winter.
problem: Contradicted by E1. The journal has a 46-day gap with no entries between 12 December 1741 and 26 January 1742, and folios 31-34 are missing.

quote: The parish register shows 52 burials in 1742, which is 23 more than in 1741.
problem: Arithmetic error. E5(a) gives 33 burials in 1741, so the difference is 19, not 23.

quote: Of the 29 death entries in the journal, Wray names a fever as the cause in seven.
problem: Wrong count. E5(b) gives fever in 5 entries (cold or frost in 6, no cause named in 18).

quote: The frost alone accounts for the rise in burials in 1742.
problem: Unsupported causal claim. E5(b) shows frost named in only 6 of 29 death entries and no cause at all in 18, so the rise in the register cannot be attributed solely to frost.

quote: Wray's burial entries have been checked against the parish register and found accurate.
problem: Overstated. E6 Q8 says the editor compared only nine burial notices and had not checked the remainder.

quote: Wray states that the vicar kept the tithe barn locked against the poor.
problem: Misrepresents Q5. The passage is hearsay ('It is said by some'), Wray says he has not seen it himself, and he notes that Mr. Hale gives out that the barn is empty.

quote: The journal gives a representative picture of how rural parishes in the county fared that winter.
problem: Unsupported. E1 says the edition covers one parish and prints no records or comparative material from any other parish.

quote: Of the 48 nurses who were screened but not randomized, most (31) declined to take part.
problem: Wrong reason. T2 gives 31 as ineligible and 17 as declined, so the 31 is the ineligible count.

quote: Across both arms, 56 of 64 participants (85.9%) completed the week 8 assessment.
problem: Arithmetic error. T2 gives 56 of 64 as 87.5%. 85.9% would correspond to 55 of 64.

quote: The reduction in insomnia severity persisted after the program ended.
problem: Unsupported. T1 and T4 show assessments only at baseline and week 8, with none after week 8, so persistence after the program cannot be shown.

quote: The sleep-restriction module is what drove the improvement.
problem: Unsupported. T7 section 3.1 says components are never delivered alone and the study does not test individual components, so no module can be credited.

quote: Engagement with the program was high.
problem: Overstated. T5 shows a median of 5 of 8 modules, 2 participants completing none, and 8 of 32 completing three or fewer. The appendix does not support 'high'.

quote: These data show the program is safe for night-shift nurses.
problem: Overstated. T6 reports only two mild events in 32 app participants, and T7 section 7.4 says the study is not powered to estimate adverse event rates.

quote: The findings apply to shift workers generally.
problem: Overgeneralised. T1 shows a single-centre study of registered nurses at one teaching hospital, with no other shift workers enrolled.

quote: Below 3.0 kN the bracket has an effectively infinite fatigue life.
problem: Unsupported extrapolation. F2 and F3 state that no specimens were tested below 3.0 kN.

quote: One of the four specimens reached the runout and the other three failed, the shortest at 1,138,000 cycles.
problem: Wrong figure. F3 gives the shortest 4.0 kN failure as F4-04 at 1,238,000 cycles.

quote: At 4.0 kN the bracket has a 75 percent chance of failing before two million cycles.
problem: Overstated. Three of four specimens failed, which is an observed frequency from n=4, and F2 states that no statistical analysis of the fatigue data was performed.

quote: The mean life at 5.0 kN was about 483,000 cycles.
problem: Arithmetic error. F3 gives 412,000, 366,000, 508,000 and 447,000 cycles, whose mean is about 433,000.

quote: The excess set in S08 is explained by its coming from a different material lot.
problem: Unsupported causal claim. The F5 log says the lot B mill certificate is not on file and no sectioning, hardness or tensile tests on lot B are scheduled, so the cause is unknown.

quote: The bracket's performance carries over to the full range of service temperatures.
problem: Unsupported. F2 says all tests ran at 20.1-22.6 C with no tests at other temperatures, while REQ-EN-003 in F1 requires operation from -30 C to +50 C.

quote: The fatigue programme was run in accordance with ASTM E466.
problem: Overstated. F1 says the method was adapted from ASTM E466 with deviations. TP-221 section 4 records four specimens per level against a plan of six and load frame alignment that was not verified.
